comment: Generated by internal/generator/engineclientgen (go test ./internal/generator/engineclientgen -run TestClientCodegenParity -update). documents are engine schemas in the order an engine defines and publishes them. For each schema, createParams is each behavior's create parameters as the generator narrows them for its config, which the engine's describe document must show in the same shape, descriptions aside; fields is each behavior field's JSON Schema as the generator types it, by behavior name, then field name, with present true for one every read holds: a read's behaviors must hold an entry for each of these behaviors and no other, and its fields must satisfy them.

documents.name: Spec
documents.description: A spec tasks pin a revision of. Its blockers are tasks, so a blocker names its schema, and it is final once a principal with specs.approve signs off.

documents.name: Task
documents.description: A task of a project: its kind picks the shape of its detail, it pins the spec it builds, it lists the tasks it relates to, it waits for its blockers, and it fails a day after it starts unless it is done.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: The task's detail, of its kind's type.

documents.name: Project
documents.description: A project its tasks link to, which rolls them up.

documents.name: Request
documents.description: A request whose category and summary a model fills (D73): a model outside the engine fills its category and summary from its subject and body, while it is new or in triage; a category under 0.8 confidence waits in review, and the request moves to assigned only once its category is reviewed.

documents.name: notes
documents.description: A note that moves from draft through review to published, collects comments, and keeps its revisions. A change to it can be proposed for an editor to approve.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Words to find the note by.

documents.name: Inventory
documents.description: Units a shop counts and prices (D70): Stock with a unit price in GBP and a reorder level.

documents.name: CollectionPoint
documents.description: A counter that opens fifteen-minute pickup slots (D70): Calendar in Europe/London, four at a time.

documents.name: Checkout
documents.description: A checkout that holds its lines' units and a pickup slot while it waits for payment (D70), and is placed once paid.

documents.name: Refund
documents.description: A refund two staff sign off before it is issued against its checkout's payment (D70).

Links.description: The links the instance holds from its create, by name, each held to link's rules.

counter.description: The CollectionPoint instance counter points at: its id.

schema.description: Each item the claim's holds ask, in hold and item order: { hold, item, schema, id, quantity or startMs and endMs, state, unitPrice?, currency? }, the supply it names, what it asks, its state (pending, held, committed, released, returned), and the unit price the supply held it at. An item's state only advances.

hold.description: The hold's name in the config.

item.description: The item's index in its hold.

quantity.description: The units it asks, of counted supply.

schema.description: The supply's schema.

startMs.description: When the time it asks starts, of timed supply.

unitPrice.description: The unit price the supply held it at, in the currency's minor units.

schema.description: The least advanced state of the items: none before any is asked, then pending, held, committed, released or returned. A rule hears it turn committed.

The sum of the priced items' unit prices times their quantities, as { amount, currency }: an item without a price adds nothing, and with none priced it is { amount: 0, currency: null }. Null only when the priced items' currencies differ or the sum passes what a JSON number holds exactly.

The links the instance holds, by name: each target's schema and id, and for a pinned link the revision or the release it records, the target's latest and whether the target has moved past it; for a many-valued link, a list of them in the order they were linked. Absent when the instance holds none.

counter.description: The CollectionPoint instance counter points at.

schema.description: The number as the format prints it, unique within its scope; absent until it is numbered.
The instance's number in its count, from 1; absent until it is numbered.
The last twenty attempts, newest first: { attempt, provider, providerRef?, amount, currency, status, authorized?, captured?, brand?, last4?, openedAt, updatedAt }.
What the provider has authorized and not voided or captured.
What the provider has captured.
The ISO 4217 code of every amount.

What the instance owes, in the currency's minor units. It does not change while an attempt is open. From Holds.total, it is 0 while the total cannot be read (an item pending, priced items in two currencies, or a sum past what an integer holds), and openPayment and require refuse with total_unknown then.
due less captured, never below 0.
What captures brought past what was due, such as a late capture of an attempt that failed while a newer one paid, which Payments asked back with a refund of it.
What the provider has refunded.
unpaid, pending (an attempt is open), authorized, paid, partiallyRefunded or refunded. A rule hears it turn paid.

Each started deadline, by name: { dueAt, fired, firedAt?, outcome? }, when it is due, in epoch milliseconds, whether it has fired and when, and what its then met: moved, skipped (the status was not one it moves from), vetoed or forbidden. A deadline not started, or cancelled, is absent. Nothing in it follows the clock: a deadline is overdue while it has not fired and its dueAt has passed.
When the status last changed, in epoch milliseconds: the create's time, then each transition's. Absent on an instance created before Workflow kept it, until its next transition.
The state the instance is in.
The closures that have not ended, soonest first, at most 100: { closure, startMs, endMs, reason }.

endMs.description: When it ends, in epoch milliseconds.

startMs.description: When it starts, in epoch milliseconds.

onHand less held: what a new hold can take. Never below 0 unless the config allows backorder.
The units claims hold and have neither committed nor released.
Whether available is at or below the config's lowAt; false without one. A list filters on it, so where Stock.low is true lists what to reorder.
The units on hand: received, adjusted and counted, less what claims committed, plus what they returned. Always the sum of the instance's movements.

Each rollup's value, by name, computed when the instance is read: a count, counts by value, a number, a field's value, or a boolean. A rollup whose link holds more than 500 instances is {"over": true} instead; a min or max with no value to compare, and a latest whose instance holds none, is absent.

tasks.description: count over the Task instances whose project points here.

schema.description: The subjects writing a message now: each subject with a composing message on the instance, once, in the order of its earliest composing message's id; empty while nobody is.

How many posted and interrupted messages the conversation has, top-level and replies; composing, deleted and purged ones are not counted.

Replies are read thread by thread, in the inbox, and not counted here.
